items.title: How do Batch Normalization and Activation Functions work together to enhance stability in ANN training?
items.content: Batch normalization normalizes input data for each layer, reducing internal covariate shift that can lead to instability during backpropagation. Activation functions introduce non-linearity into the network, allowing it to learn more complex relationships between inputs. Together, batch normalization helps stabilize the training process and activation functions provide the necessary non-linearity to enable learning.

items.title: What is the relationship between Deep Learning and Supervised Learning?
items.content: Deep learning is a subset of machine learning that specializes in supervised learning tasks, where artificial neural networks learn from labeled datasets to predict outputs. In supervised learning, the network is trained to minimize the error between predicted and actual outputs, allowing it to learn the underlying patterns in the data.

items.title: Can CNNs be used for tasks beyond image and video analysis?
items.content: While convolutional neural networks (CNNs) were originally designed for image and video analysis, they can also be used for other tasks such as audio analysis, natural language processing, and even control systems. This is due to the ability of CNNs to extract features from data that are invariant to transformations, making them a versatile tool in deep learning.

items.title: How does the concept of Transfer Learning impact the performance of a new machine learning model?
items.content: Transfer learning allows pre-trained models' weights to be used as a starting point for a new, but related task. This can significantly improve the performance of a new model by leveraging the knowledge and features learned from the pre-training data, reducing the need for large amounts of labeled training data.

items.title: What are some potential drawbacks of using Reinforcement Learning with ANNs?
items.content: One potential drawback of using reinforcement learning with artificial neural networks (ANNs) is the need for a large amount of labeled data or expert knowledge to specify the reward function, which can be time-consuming and expensive. Additionally, the training process can be highly unstable due to the exploration-exploitation trade-off, requiring careful tuning of hyperparameters and regularization techniques.
